chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Saeed narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hamdan al-Qushairi, from al-Mughira ibn Muhammad ibn al-Muhallab al-Azdi, from Abdul-Ghaffar ibn Muhammad al-Kelabi, from Amr ibn Thabit, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father (peace be upon them):

He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: My love and the love of my Ahl al-Bayt is beneficial in seven situations whose horrors are great: at death, in the grave, at the Resurrection, at the Recording, at the Reckoning, at the Balance, and at the Path.
ai.seo_question: What are the seven moments in the afterlife where love for the Prophet and his family is beneficial?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Fadail al-Shia* underscores the centrality of *mawadda* (affection) for the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt as a decisive factor in the individual's spiritual survival during the seven distinct stages of the afterlife, from the pangs of death to the final crossing of the Sirat. It reflects the Shia theological emphasis that love is not merely an emotional state but a transformative force that alleviates the terrors of the grave and facilitates a favorable judgment, aligning with the concept of *Shafa'ah* (intercession) granted to the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.badr-shahin: Al-Hasan bin Abdullah bin Saeed narrated to us from Mohammed bin Ahmed bin Hamdan al-Qushairi from al-Mugheera bin Mohammed bin al-Muhallab al-Azdi from Abdul-Ghaffar bin Mohammed al-Kelabi from Amir bin Thabit from Jabir that Abu Ja’far related on the authority of Ali bin al-Hussein from his father (a)

that the Prophet (s) said: The love for my household and me will help in seven situations whose horrors are enormous: at death, in the grave, in the Resurrection, in the Recorded Account, in the Judgment, in the Balance, and on the Path.
